title: Handoff: tests, packaging and a report for finance

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A refactoring keeps every rule test passing but moves forty units to other years. Which test of this lesson notices?

options.text: A rule test, since a moved unit breaks some budget row
options.says: The page: none of the rule tests would notice such a move.

options.text: The declaration test, since the version has to change
options.says: The page: that test reads pyproject.toml and `__version__`, never a plan, so it passes.

options.text: The golden report test, since the reviewed plan moved
options.says: Right: the report no longer equals the reviewed golden file.

options.text: The repeat-run test, since two runs now disagree
options.says: The page: two runs of the changed code still write the same report, so it passes.

origin.section: The Code Prints for Its Author, Not for Finance

questions.stem: Why does the golden test solve a 30-unit fleet exactly, rather than keep the 500-unit report solved to a 2% gap?

options.text: The 500-unit run is infeasible at 2%, so its report can't be kept
options.says: It finished OPTIMAL, within 1.70% of its bound.

options.text: A run stopped at 2% could keep any plan within that gap
options.says: Right: a harmless change in the search could move the plan it stops at.

options.text: The 30-unit fleet is real data, unlike the 500-unit one
options.says: Both fleets are generated; the report says the data are fictional.

options.text: The 500-unit report has no bound line, so it can't be checked
options.says: Its last line states the bound and the gap.

origin.section: The Tests Guard the Numbers, the Report, Repeatability and the Declaration

questions.stem: The solver returns OPTIMAL for a run stopped at a 2% gap. How does the finance report put the plan's quality?

options.text: It calls the plan optimal, since the solver's status says so
options.says: The report keeps the status but states the bound, because finance reads optimal as best.

options.text: It reports the objective alone, since finance reads money
options.says: Its last line gives the bound and how close the plan is.

options.text: It gives the gap to the first year's LP relaxation
options.says: The gap is to the bound of the whole plan's solve.

options.text: It states the bound and how close the plan is to that bound
options.says: Right: what the run proved, in finance's terms.

origin.section: Design Note: The Report States the Bound, Not "Optimal"

concepts: why the golden run is small and exact
which test notices a plan that moved without breaking a rule
how the report states a plan's quality
